Fixed: the economy example is now a 2012 Toyota Corolla whose low price is on a page that says new and names 2009-2013 Corolla fitment; the midsize example is now a 2015 Subaru Forester 2.5i, whose rear muffler is a separate bolt-on part and which has a book time for the example vehicle. Every aftermarket page loaded for them failed one test: no model years in the page text (stockwiseauto.com Walker 50063, 50464, 54767; Bosal 229-005), fitment for other years only (Walker 54767 is 2006-2008 Forester, Walker 50063 is 2006-2008 Ram 1500 on the pages that print years), no statement that the part is new (autobarn.net Walker 53729, americantrucks.com C&L R111019), or no price (napaonline.com BRExhaust 106-0596). unit: per job: one rear muffler, fitted, as a bolt-on or direct-fit assembly the way it is sold for the vehicle (on many cars the rear muffler comes welded to its tail pipe as one piece). Low = a direct-fit aftermarket muffler, high = the genuine part at list (MSRP). Not included: other pipes, a second muffler on cars with two, the resonator, the catalytic converter, hangers, gaskets and clamps, and cutting or welding of custom pipe

finding: Held: this file is not ready to publish. There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so there is nothing to call too wide or too narrow; this is a first build. What can be built (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2012 Toyota Corolla about $206-$740 (parts $146.26-$595.67, 0.5-0.9 hour). For the other three classes only the top can be built, because no aftermarket price passed the sourcing test: midsize 2015 Subaru Forester 2.5i up to about $583 (genuine muffler $439.45, 0.6-0.9 hour); truck 2015 Ram 1500 5.7L up to about $1,152 (genuine $832, 0.9-2 hours); luxury 2012 Lexus ES 350 up to about $821 for one of its two rear mufflers (genuine $676.97, 0.5-0.9 hour). The part is most of every total: the labor is roughly $60 to $320. What is null and why: the low parts price for the midsize, truck and luxury examples. Direct-fit aftermarket mufflers are sold for all three, and prices of roughly $110-$190 were seen, but each page failed one test: it printed no model years, listed other years only, did not say the part was new, or showed no price. Those prices are kept as cross-checks and are not used. How solid the labor times are: two examples have a time for the example vehicle, and neither is a maker document. The Forester's 0.6 hour is a Subaru book time quoted by a named mechanic, and the Ram's 2 hours is a parts seller's figure written for an owner fitting a bolt-on muffler at home (a second seller listing for the same truck says 1 hour). Every other range end is a maker-stated time for a different vehicle: Hyundai's 0.5 hour for the centre muffler on the 2014-2015 Tucson and FCA's 0.9 hour for the muffler on the 2015 Ram 2500 and 3500 5.7L. No maker-stated time with a unit was found for the Corolla, Forester, Ram 1500 or ES 350. Four maker figures support the range without being used as ends because each includes an inspection or prints no unit: Mazda 0.4 hour (2019 CX-5 Turbo), FCA 0.3 hour (2020 Jeep Cherokee, inspect and replace), Kia 0.4 hour (2023 Sportage centre muffler, inspect and replace) and Subaru 0.2 with no unit (2015-2017 Legacy and Outback). These suggest warranty times are often shorter than 0.5 hour, so the labor range here is not low. All of them are times for bolted joints that come apart; a rusted flange or seized bolts on an older car add time, and the 0.9 hour top does not allow for that. On some vehicles the larger main muffler is part of a centre pipe that costs far more from the maker and is outside this unit; a quote for 'a muffler' on such a vehicle may be for that part. Benchmarks: RepairPal's national average is $1,138-$1,190 with parts at about $1,035, far above the built totals, while its Corolla figure ($625-$661) sits inside the built economy range and its Silverado and F-150 figures ($706-$830) sit under the built truck top. The national figure appears to price a dearer genuine part or a larger exhaust section; the page does not say which, so that is a reading, not a finding. Only RepairPal could be loaded as a full-cost benchmark (the third entry is parts only), short of the three independent estimates asked for; a search for others returned only unsigned cost-guide pages that are not cited. Confidence is low because three low parts prices are missing, half the labor range ends are not for the example vehicle and no example has a maker-stated time. This is an estimate, not a quote and not a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds new gaskets, clamps, bolts and rubber hangers, and labor to cut or heat rusted fasteners. Many shops recommend replacing the connecting pipe or resonator at the same time, and on cars with two rear mufflers the second one. If no bolt-on part is used, a muffler shop may cut the old one out and weld in a universal muffler, which is priced differently from this estimate. Also possible: a diagnosis or exhaust leak check fee, shop supplies and sales tax. A muffler replaced under a recall, service campaign or warranty extension is done by the dealer at no charge, so check for open campaigns first. An exhaust leak ahead of the muffler can let fumes into the cabin and should be looked at promptly.
